items.stem: In the five-step revenue model, what must an entity do immediately after identifying the contract with a customer?

options.text: Identify the separate performance obligations in the contract
options.rationale: Correct: step 2 is identifying the distinct performance obligations.

options.text: Recognise the entire transaction price as revenue
options.rationale: Recognition is the final step, only as obligations are satisfied.

options.text: Determine the entity's income tax on the contract
options.rationale: Tax is outside the revenue model.

options.text: Write off any expected contract costs
options.rationale: Cost treatment is not the next step in the model.

items.explanation: Correct: step 2 is identifying the distinct performance obligations.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO factors indicate that a performance obligation is satisfied over time rather than at a point in time? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits as the entity performs
options.rationale: Correct: this is one of the over-time criteria.

options.text: The entity's performance creates an asset with no alternative use and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for work completed to date
options.rationale: Correct: this combination is an over-time criterion.

options.text: The customer pays the full price in advance
options.rationale: Advance payment does not by itself determine timing of recognition.

options.text: The contract includes a fixed price
options.rationale: A fixed price is unrelated to whether control transfers over time.

items.explanation: Correct: this is one of the over-time criteria.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A retailer earns a fixed fee for arranging sales of a manufacturer's goods and never controls the goods. How should it most likely recognise revenue?

options.text: As an agent, recognising only the net fee for arranging the sale
options.rationale: Correct: without control of the goods the retailer is an agent and recognises the net commission.

options.text: As a principal, recognising the gross selling price of the goods
options.rationale: Gross (principal) treatment requires control of the goods before transfer.

options.text: Not at all, because arranging sales is never revenue
options.rationale: Arranging sales for a fee is revenue; the question is gross vs net.

options.text: Only when the manufacturer is paid
options.rationale: Timing is driven by satisfying the obligation, not the manufacturer's receipt.

items.explanation: Correct: without control of the goods the retailer is an agent and recognises the net commission.
